newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway formally awards Barents licences.
newsitem.headline: Norway formally awards Barents licences.

text.p: Norway on Friday formally awarded oil exploration licences in seven areas of the Barents Sea region to 10 companies, a spokeswoman for the Oil and Energy Ministry said.
She said the companies had accepted the awards and that they were confirmed at a cabinet meeting chaired by King Harald.
The ministry two weeks ago invited the companies to take part in the Barents project. Three of the licences are normal exploration/development awards while four are for so-called seismic areas.
The companies are Norsk Hydro, Elf Petroleum, Saga Petroleum, Agip, Mobil, Phillips Petroleum, Enterprise, Neste, Amerada Hess and Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil).

Although there have been several finds in the Barents Sea since exploration began in 1980, no economic discoveries have been made so far. But the ministry has said there is still reason to believe that considerable oil and gas resources are hidden in the Barents Sea.
